items.summary: NVIDIA introduced RTX Spark, a Windows PC platform aimed at AI development and gaming in slim laptops and compact desktops. Built on Blackwell RTX GPU and Grace CPU with up to 128 GB of unified memory, it supports DLSS technologies including Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, launching with NBA 2K27. The platform features NVIDIA ACE for responsive AI characters via the Nemotron model, RTX Kit SDKs for neural rendering, Nsight tools for Arm64 optimization, and Unreal Engine 5.8 support. NVIDIA highlighted performance improvements in its latest DLSS updates while providing developers resources to integrate these technologies into their projects.
items.title: NVIDIA Unveils RTX Spark Platform for AI-Driven Gaming

items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron-Personas datasets for France and Belgium to help developers fine-tune open language models with local knowledge. Built in partnership with Pleias and KU Leuven, the persona-grounded data lets agents reflect regional priorities. The article illustrates how a base model gives an unspecific passport answer while a post-trained version provides accurate details like home visits instead of mail submission and €43 fees for French Guiana residents versus €86 elsewhere. NVIDIA describes the workflow as reusable across markets through swapped datasets, behavior contracts, and reviewers. Pleias notes better grounded data makes small regional models viable, though grounding improves coverage without guaranteeing fairness.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Persona Datasets for Fine-Tuning Regional AI Assistants

items.summary: NVIDIA and Oracle announced plans to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Superclusters with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems to multi-gigawatt scale, supporting customer demand for AI training, inference and agentic applications. The companies also made the general availability of these systems and NVIDIA Vera CPUs on OCI. Customers can scale CPU and GPU resources independently to reduce idle capacity. OpenAI has trained GPT-6 Astra on an OCI Supercluster with more than 100,000 Blackwell GPUs. Sreekanth Pothanis said infrastructure must keep pace with advancing models, while Uday Ruddarraju noted Vera CPUs deliver performance for agentic workloads.
items.title: NVIDIA and Oracle Expand AI Infrastructure Partnership on OCI

items.summary: IBM and Kaggle are partnering on ScarfBench, an open benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can migrate enterprise Java applications across frameworks while preserving working behavior. The latest evaluation covered 204 migration tasks; Gemini 4 Argon with Antigravity led the primary smoke-test metric at 75.2%, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 + Claude Code at 70.5%. Though several configurations compiled nearly every task, behavioral fidelity proved a stronger discriminator than compilation: of 745 failing runs, about 72% were runtime failures. Kaggle consulted on the design, independently reproduced and sponsored compute for the evaluation, and will maintain the benchmark as new models are released. Public model submission is not available at launch but is planned.
items.title: IBM and Kaggle Launch Living ScarfBench Java Migration Leaderboard

items.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Genie 4, an updated world model that improves on its predecessor in nearly every respect. Unlike the earlier version, which drew criticism from gaming companies for resembling video games, Google frames it as a step toward artificial general intelligence. The new model generates virtual environments frame by frame in real time and draws on Gemini 3.8 Flash to guide simulations. DeepMind notes that consistency still fades after only about two minutes before contexts are forgotten.
items.title: DeepMind Unveils Genie 4 World Model With Improved Physics and Human Simulation

items.summary: A cybersecurity startup called Cathedral, run by former Department of Government Efficiency members, claims it breached internal data and messaging systems at Anthropic in less than 12 hours. The company said the intrusion exploited ordinary enterprise software vulnerabilities. Anthropic confirmed a limited set of systems was accessed and has since shut down those access points.
items.title: Former DOGE Staffers Say They Hacked Anthropic in Under 12 Hours

items.summary: On October 27, 2026, Ali Behrouz and Vahab Mirrokni of Google Research introduced a sleep framework that adds an offline memory-consolidation phase to continual learning. The authors argue deployed large language models remain static after pre-training and suffer catastrophic forgetting when updated with new data. Their approach alternates active interaction with offline consolidation using self-generated practice examples, mirroring human NREM and REM sleep. Reported results include 48.9% on single-task SQuAD and 46.2% on continued pre-training evaluations, near-perfect scaling to 10M tokens on BABILong, and reasoning scores of 79.2%, 69.0%, and 46.1% on AIME 24/25 and HMMT 25 benchmarks.
items.title: Google Research Introduces Sleep Framework for Continual Learning in LLMs

items.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band Windows updates on October 26 removing seven certificates tied to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys, which had been recoverable almost instantly because their values were smaller than 256. The update removes six eMudhra G3 roots and an AAA Certificate Services cross-sign from the Windows trust list for systems without Internet access or automatic updates. Microsoft explained that removing a root is broader than blocking the compromised intermediate keys, so organizations with compatibility needs may choose to trust certificates locally after their own security assessment.
items.title: Microsoft Removes Compromised eMudhra Certificates From Windows Trust List

items.summary: Google DeepMind released its newest world model, Genie 4, in research preview Tuesday, generating the most photorealistic and interactive worlds yet alongside real-time audio. Research director Tejas Kulkarni described hybrid models combining Gemini writing code with Genie simulating reality at different abstraction levels during a briefing. Diego Rivas noted trusted testers may use it for prototyping films, though he stressed early development remains ongoing.
items.title: Google DeepMind Unveils Genie 4 World Model With Real-Time Audio

items.summary: Databricks announced Vital Skills, an open-source set of packaged playbooks built in the Agent Skills standard that equip its Genie Code coding agent with healthcare and life sciences domain knowledge. The skills integrate with Unity Catalog so generated code follows Databricks security and governance rules. Testing on BiomniBench showed Genie Code alone rarely failed obvious tasks but sometimes fell short on domain-specific methodology; with Vital Skills it scored higher without harming out-of-scope tasks. On a TEDDY single-cell model deployment task, the baseline completed 19 of 27 checks while all 27 completed with the skill.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Vital Skills for Healthcare and Life Sciences

items.summary: Meta describes PrivacyLib, a common library that runs inside its clients of hundreds of data and processing systems to enforce privacy requirements like purpose limitation. It replaces per-system enforcement with shared modules evaluated billions of checks every second while consuming only a small fraction of Meta’s compute.
items.title: Meta’s PrivacyLib Enforces Data-Access Controls at Scale

items.summary: The 2026 Python Typing Survey received 1,794 responses. Its main finding is that checker selection changed sharply while type hint use stayed steady across three years. The share selecting makes AI-generated code more accurate/reliable rose from 18.5% in 2025 to 38.4% in 2026; AI tools wrote hints for 42.5% of respondents, and 61.0% used at least one listed option. Missing library type information led difficulties (65.1%), with better callable syntax the top missing feature (45.7%). The Pyrefly team noted it is already studying how AI tools and checkers interact, leaving which interactions actually help an open question.
items.title: 2026 Python Typing Survey Finds AI Tools and Checkers Reshaping Type Work

items.summary: A Databricks post describes improving document extraction accuracy with ai_extract and MLflow Prompt Registry, based on a project extracting roughly 40 structured fields from partner-submitted order documents across dozens of PDF layouts. Reviewers corrected approved values before downstream use, giving human-reviewed ground truth for evaluation. The authors found that fixing one field can regress others; in their testing total extraction errors increased by 9% while the revision field improved. They recommend schema descriptions for field rules and global instructions for document-level reasoning, using code to normalize output rather than the model. ai_extract version 2.1 precision mode reduces over-extraction on repeated structures but does not fix definition problems like a status term instead of a number. Citations show where answers were found; confidence scores rank review without gating quality. MLflow Prompt Registry versions prompts and schemas separately from code, using aliases for prod, candidate, and experimental versions. A fixed cohort of several hundred PDFs is scored repeatedly to establish a noise floor, with verdicts like BETTER or INCONCLUSIVE guiding human-controlled promotion rather than automatic shipping.
items.title: Databricks Documents AI Extract Accuracy Improvement Workflow Post

items.summary: Thailand’s car production fell 6.08% in September from a year earlier, the Federation of Thai Industries (FTI) said on Oct 27, reaching 120,319 units after an August rise of 10.93%. The FTI noted that automakers and parts suppliers had resumed operations following flooding that killed at least 80 people in September. Domestic sales rose 14.28%, driven by electric vehicles, while exports climbed 4.55% year on year. The federation kept its annual production target at 1.45 million units after cutting it from the 1.5 million set for start of 2026.
items.title: Thai Auto Output Falls as Flood Recovery Underpins September Sales

items.summary: Ai2 released Old Ideas, Novel Problems, a study of how reliably large language models judge the novelty of scientific research ideas. The team built an automated pipeline around ICLR 2026 peer reviews to create high- and low-novelty pools of human-authored ideas. Testing six LLM judges, they found that small prompt changes shifted accuracy by more than 50 percentage points on AI-generated ideas, while retrieval and extra reasoning did not consistently help; purpose-built evaluators scored lower at higher cost. The authors conclude novelty evaluation remains an open problem and offer their benchmark as a starting point for building more robust methods.
items.title: Ai2 Releases Benchmark Questioning Whether LLMs Can Judge Research Novelty

items.summary: Pang Chong Liu submitted a forum post proposing stronger community support for school emergency preparedness, prompted by an Oct 22 drill at Bukit Batok Secondary School. He suggested adding neighbourhood coordination to selected drills so schools and local police centres can improve reporting of concerns, information flow to parents, and keeping access clear for emergency vehicles.
items.title: Community Support for School Emergency Preparedness Proposed

items.summary: Pop Mart International Group reported a decline in third-quarter revenue from a year earlier, driven by weakening Labubu momentum and a strong prior-year comparison after blockbuster results. Overall revenue fell as much as 50%, down from growth of about 250% the previous period. China sales declined 25% to 30%, while Americas sales fell 70% to 75%. HSBC Holdings cut its 2027 and 2028 forecasts by 8% and 9%, lowering its 2026 estimate to 33.2 billion yuan (S$6.4 billion) from 34.6 billion, citing a longer road to stabilisation.
items.title: Pop Mart sales plunge up to 50% amid fading Labubu demand

items.summary: Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang joined the Latent Space podcast to describe how Anthropic builds its Claude Platform, including launching Claude Opus 5.5, separating a model’s reasoning from an agent’s actions, scaling APIs, and managing agents through decoupled brain, harness and sandbox components. The episode also covers an interview with Anthropic about its S-1 filing, revenue per employee, improvement loops, training incidents versus production safeguards, distillation, benchmarks, managed-agent memory and safety classifiers.
items.title: Anthropic engineers explain Claude Platform safety and Opus 5.5 launch on Latent Space podcast

items.summary: OpenAI released an acknowledgements page for Genie 4, described as a new generation of world simulation. The text lists core contributors and cross-functional partners by name across several sentences spanning the document, then thanks Raia Hadsell, Aäron van den Oord, Josh Woodward, Steve Seitz, Carlos Hernandez, Elias Roman, Jung E. Kim, Abhishek Bapna, Eli Collins, Tulsee Doshi, Carolina Parada, Jie Tan, Koray Kavukcuoglu and Demis Hassabis for guidance, and finally thanks testers and early access users for feedback.
items.title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world-simulation model

items.summary: A Chinese research collaboration released a tool that accepts natural language prompts to produce proteins with specified functions, though success rates may be low because users must still understand enzyme mechanisms, amino acid positions, and water molecules. Hugging Face separately announced hosting a similar DNA-level tool. The author compares the development to vibe coding, noting it works only where labs can separate successful designs from many failures.
items.title: Vibe coding arrives for protein and genome design software

items.summary: According to an Nvidia blog post, Firebird.ai has obtained an export license for 45,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs for a data center built with Kazakhtelecom. The first phase is under construction, with launch set for the third quarter of 2027; capacity could reach 500 megawatts after a planned second phase. Huang visited Kazakhstan in October to discuss AI collaboration.
items.title: Nvidia Clears 45,000 Blackwell GPUs for Kazakhstan Data Center

items.summary: XPENG ranked highest in the European USCALE “EV Satisfaction Study” for the second consecutive year, according to CleanTechnica reporting. Its 82% recommendation rate improved over the previous year and ranks significantly above the 53% industry average, placing XPENG ahead of American, European and Asian manufacturers. The Stuttgart-based study surveyed over 4000 customers from Germany, Austria and Switzerland using Net Promotor Score methodology. Tesla took second place while Opel, Fiat and MG ranked lowest. USCALE’s Axel Sprenger noted EV drivers are more satisfied yet more demanding, with competition now decided by software and charging experience.
items.title: XPENG Tops European EV Satisfaction Ranking for Second Year

items.summary: A University of North Florida poll found that, when asked to choose between protecting the environment and economic growth, likely voters favored the environment by more than 2 to 1. Sixty-one percent said officials should prioritize the environment even at the risk of curbing economic growth; 26 percent chose growth. Registered Republicans sided with the environment 48 percent to 35 percent. The result arrives in a tight Florida Senate race between incumbent Ashley Moody and Angie Nixon, weeks before Election Day. Analysts caution that data center rules and power rates are largely set in Tallahassee rather than Washington.
items.title: Florida Voters Favor Environment Over Growth in Moody-Nixon Race

items.summary: HydroWing Ltd, Inyanga Marine Energy Group's tidal division, signed a contract with Ecodetect to add AI-driven environmental monitoring to its Morlais tidal stream project off Anglesey. The 30 MW scheme will use real-time sensors and cameras to detect marine life and trigger mitigation protocols while building compliance evidence for UK, EU and international standards. Richard Parkinson said the technology balances performance and ecological responsibility; Dr David Gold called it a chance for Inyanga to lead on environmental protection.
items.title: HydroWing Signs Ecodetect AI Monitoring Deal for Morlais Tidal Project

items.summary: On October 27, the Federal Communications Commission approved Amazon Leo’s $11.57 billion deal to acquire Globalstar. The agency announced Tuesday that it has cleared the transaction. Amazon Leo has launched more than 300 satellites since April 2025 and plans to deploy about 3,200 satellites in Earth's low orbit by 2029. Through the acquisition, Amazon adds Globalstar's two dozen satellites to its existing network of more than 200.
items.title: FCC Approves Amazon Leo’s Globalstar Acquisition

items.summary: Oracle announced on Tuesday it is expanding its cloud AI chip agreements with Nvidia while adding offerings from Alphabet's Google and Cerebras Systems. The company will deploy Nvidia's Vera Rubin servers at multi-gigawatt scale but use Oracle's own Acceleron networking chips for some systems, and begin offering Google TPUs for the first time. Mahesh Thiagarajan of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure said different AI workloads have different compute needs, giving customers flexibility to choose infrastructure suited to each workload's performance, throughput and economics.
items.title: Oracle Broadens AI Chip Partnerships With Nvidia, Google and Cerebras

items.summary: An analysis of Anthropic's IPO prospectus frames it as an ink-blot test, dividing reactions between believers who see a fast-growing company backed by blue-chip firms with $131 billion in cash, and skeptics who point to rising losses. Skeptics highlight at least $542 billion in future data-center lease and chip payments appearing only in footnotes, plus $81 billion in net losses suggesting costs shifted onto investors.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO prospectus divides investors into believers and skeptics

items.summary: In its IPO prospectus filed Monday, Anthropic told potential investors that rising energy costs could slow the company's AI buildout if it cannot secure power access. The filing notes contracts may force it to pay for grid upgrades even when capacity is delayed or unrealized, and warns of wildfire risks from climate change. Anthropic also disclosed roughly $400 billion in chip purchases and data center leases, plus an $81 billion loss in the first half of this year.
items.title: Anthropic Warns Energy Costs May Slow AI Expansion

items.summary: Anthropic filed its registration statement with the SEC on October 26, seeking a Nasdaq listing under ticker ANT. The offering price and share count remain undisclosed, while market reports place potential valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. The debut draws attention to both generative AI's commercial opportunity and risks from increasingly powerful systems.
items.title: Anthropic's AI IPO Faces Commercial and Existential Scrutiny

items.summary: The UK's official minimum wage rates rose on 1 April, affecting about 2.7 million workers nationwide. From that date, the National Living Wage for those over 21 is £12.71 an hour - up 50p from 2025, or roughly £900 more a year for someone working full time at 37.5 hours a week. The rate for 18-to-20-year-olds reached £10.85 an hour, and the minimum wage for 16-and-17-year-olds is now £8 an hour. A rise in the Budget on Wednesday may bring 18-to-20 year-olds to around £11.27 an hour, matching over-20s - a break from recent government efforts to end age-based pay disparity.
items.title: UK Minimum Wage Rates Rise for Millions of Workers

items.summary: A news feature previews six charts underpinning John Healey’s first budget as chancellor, set against the cost of living crisis and Middle East-driven inflation. The Resolution Foundation estimates fiscal headroom has been halved to about £12bn from £23.6bn, with at least £14bn needed to avoid a bond market reaction. Pledged “breathing space” measures include more than £1bn for energy consumers, as household energy bills are forecast to rise to £2,000 a year by January. Devolution plans offer mayors a new £1.5bn borrowing facility. Defence spending is targeted at 3% of GDP by 2030, with the Institute for Fiscal Studies estimating an extra £11bn needed that year. The piece also covers youth unemployment and Brexit’s economic impact on net migration estimates.
items.title: Budget 2026 charts preview economic pressures on UK chancellor

items.summary: Opinion writer Nils Pratley argues that the two state-funded investment bodies, the National Wealth Fund and the British Business Bank, deserve more oversight after chancellor John Healey increased their capital. The article notes £15.4bn extra for the NWF over five years on top of its existing £27.8bn, plus another £5bn for the BBB, which already has £30.6bn. It flags concerns that the bodies may blur their additionality role and cites examples such as a £25m Kraken Technologies investment within a wider $1bn raise, alongside calls from the Centre for Policy Studies to limit PuFin use. The author suggests an Office for Budget Responsibility-style body could help police judgments on additionality, while acknowledging that policing them is equally important as ensuring they stay true to their brief.
items.title: Column Questions Scrutiny of Chancellor's PuFin Investment Boost

items.summary: Blake Mackenzie, a 12-year-old student in Newcastle, won the 2026 Australian Poetry Slam Youth Champion title after his teacher encouraged him to enter. He advanced through local and state heats before performing at the Sydney Opera House finals alongside adult champion Bivor of Alice Springs. The pair share a $20,000 prize package as 2026 Australian Poetry Slambassadors. Mackenzie's poems addressed racism in Australia and AI's impact on daily life.
items.title: Twelve-year-old Blake Mackenzie wins national slam poetry title with AI-themed poem

items.summary: Official data released Tuesday showed that China's major industrial firms posted a double-digit profit increase for the first nine months of 2026, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). Profits climbed 15.5% year on year to 6.03 trillion yuan (about $900 billion) in January-September, with electronics and high-tech manufacturing as key drivers. Electronics profits doubled from a year earlier, contributing 9.6% to the overall rise; high-tech manufacturing surged 52%, outpacing the industrial average by 36.5%. NBS statistician Yu Weining noted that China's industrial sector is shifting toward an innovation-driven structure.
items.title: China's industrial profits rose as electronics and high-tech manufacturing led growth in early 2026

items.summary: Government insiders told The Guardian that the giant Rosebank oilfield could be approved without breaching the UK’s emission targets, boosting cabinet colleagues lobbying for approval. Energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh had leaned toward rejecting it, but chancellor John Healey and others argue emissions from exported oil no longer count against domestic budgets. Greenpeace and Friends of Earth urged consideration of cumulative impacts on North Sea drilling. Experts estimate Rosebank could emit 1m additional tonnes of carbon dioxide by 2042, against an overall limit of 90m tonnes. Climate researcher Greg Muttitt said approving it is not inconsistent with UK commitments since most oil will be exported and count toward other countries’ emissions.
items.title: UK Government Insiders Say Rosebank Can Be Approved Without Breaching Emission Targets

items.summary: A Warwick crown court heard that a 13-month-old girl, Isabella Stasiak, was fatally injured by her mother after suffering physical and sexual abuse. Michal Stasiak, 28, and Kinga Wydrzynska, 26, pleaded not guilty to 11 counts related to the death. Emergency services found Isabella grey and lifeless on 7 January 2025; medical experts said she died from a forceful impact to her head. The trial continues.
items.title: Parents Charged Over Fatal Abuse of Baby Girl

items.summary: An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state found they died from severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and officers failing to respond to distress calls. Forensic evidence showed acute respiratory failure aggravated by heat stress and dehydration, not a disease outbreak as initially claimed. The detainees were held on suspicion of illegal mining after an unapproved raid.
items.title: Nigeria Inquiry Finds Detention Deaths Preventable

items.summary: Twin brothers Jamal and Kamal Abubakari from Ghana and American Amanda Joy Opoku-Boachie pleaded guilty to joining an international network that defrauded people on dating sites and social media. The group targeted elderly victims in the US and Europe with fake identities, directing them toward bank accounts in Ghana; between July 2024 and April 2026 the victims collectively lost $9m (£6.7m). The three face up to 20 years and will be sentenced next year.
items.title: Ghanaian twins and US woman plead guilty over romance scam

items.summary: A coalition of academics, engineers, artists and activists selected by student assemblies defeated Aleksandar Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party in Sunday's parliamentary elections. The Student List won the popular vote and most seats; it will choose its next prime minister rather than field a traditional party. Analysts Branislav Radeljic, Nebojsa Vladisavljevic and Ana Jovic-Lazic credit nearly two years of student-led protests since November 2024 with turning mobilisation into institutional change through decentralised decision-making. The movement's leaderless structure has made it hard for the ruling party to discredit, though Radeljic warns whether its practices can deliver effective government remains unproven.
items.title: Student Assemblies Topple Serbia’s Ruling Party

items.summary: Negotiations are set to begin on the world’s first international protocol against environmental crime, including wildlife trafficking, illegal deforestation and illicit waste smuggling. The resolution was approved Oct. 23 at UNTOC’s 13th biennial gathering under the treaty established in 2003. Put forward by 12 countries led by Brazil with over a two-thirds majority of 83 votes for against 12, it will be drafted over two years to ease investigation and prosecution.
items.title: Countries Begin Drafting Global Environmental Crime Protocol

items.summary: Police charged a 46-year-old man with using false, misleading material and making a false representation after allegedly claiming he was injured in last December's Bondi massacre. Fifteen people were killed when the attack struck attendees at a Jewish festival celebrating Hanukkah.
items.title: Man charged over false Bondi terror attack injury claim

items.summary: Egypt’s parliament approved on Monday authorising President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military assistance to defend Saudi Arabia if requested, passing with the required two-thirds majority. The decision allows measures to protect Saudi territory and holy sites but does not specify what help would be given or confirm troops were sent. Egypt’s Social Democratic Party urged abstention over lack of detail on scope, cost and risks. Meanwhile, Houthi attacks continued as regional officials met in Tehran to prevent escalation.
items.title: Egypt’s Parliament Authorises Conditional Military Aid for Saudi Arabia Amid Houthi Attacks

items.summary: An Iraqi court sentenced seven French nationals on Tuesday for belonging to the Islamic State group, a court statement said. Six men received life imprisonment under Iraqi law, equivalent to 20 years; Amza Benabed got 15 years. They had been held in Syria until last year and transferred to Iraq to stand trial. The seventh defendant is among more than 5,700 detainees moved from north-eastern Syria after January clashes.
items.title: Iraq Sentences Seven French Nationals for Islamic State Links

items.summary: French lawmakers held a minute of silence for Pengo Bossio Wangi, who died in last week's shooting. At least five other people were wounded, including a 12-year-old girl. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports from the ground.
items.title: French Lawmakers Observe Silence for Racist Attack Victim

items.summary: Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said on Tuesday that the country's real GDP growth would have exceeded 8 per cent but for external shocks over the last three years. She noted India grew at over 7 per cent in an inconducive environment, and added up to 1 percentage point could be immediately added if conditions improve.
items.title: India could have achieved over 8% GDP growth without external shocks: RBI Deputy Governor

items.summary:
Shawn Mrzena, a former Microsoft director from Redmond, Washington, left the company after nearly 26 years under its July 2026 voluntary retirement offer. In his first 90 days outside corporate work he took up construction, plumbing, outdoor-gear design, fabrication and fly-fishing guiding, documenting the period on LinkedIn with a post titled “From Corporate Director to… Well, Everything Else. ” He said these months taught him more than his time at Microsoft did. Mrzena has not committed to any activity as a permanent career; he plans to decide his next move in 2027 and describes the interim as six months of family adventures and building projects. The article notes this followed an earlier programme, distinct from a separate Voluntary Exit Offer launched October 26, 2026 for employees at level 70 and below across India, the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada.

The piece is written by Anjali Thakur of Mint.
items.title: Microsoft Director Shawn Mrzena Trades Corporate Strategy for Construction and Plumbing

items.summary: Microsoft announced a time-limited Voluntary Exit offer providing financial support and career-planning resources to eligible employees in the US, UK, Canada and India. The article explains that departing staff need not withdraw retirement savings immediately; balances above $7,000 can stay until age 73 or action is taken, while other funds may roll over into an IRA or Roth IRA. A distribution of vested balances becomes available 30 days after employment ends.
items.title: Microsoft's Voluntary Exit Offer and 401(k) Options for Departing Employees

items.summary: On Monday, at Verizon's third-quarter earnings call, Dan Schulman said SpaceX would need $300 billion = 300000000000 to $500 billion = 500000000000, up to 80,000 cell towers and as long as eight years to match Verizon's network. Elon Musk replied on X: 'Will take 2 or 3 years.' Schulman said satellites alone cannot compete in cities and suburbs, about 98% of revenue, where the ground network is between 100 to 1000 times more efficient; SpaceX would need 65,000 to 80,000 large tower sites. Starlink Mobile plans to switch on in early 2028.
items.title: SpaceX CEO replies in six words to Verizon's eight-year warning

items.summary: Boeing cut its target for delivering 500 737 Max jets this year, sending shares to an 18-month low after a drop of up to 10%. The company also expects 787 Dreamliner deliveries near the lower end of guidance. It now plans to raise monthly production to 52 jets in the second half of next year from 47 currently. Chief Executive Officer Kelly Ortberg said on an analyst call that getting the ramp right matters more than timing, while Bloomberg Intelligence's George Ferguson noted it pushes cash flow expectations later.
items.title: Boeing Trims Jet Delivery Goal as Shares Slide

items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was reelected in 2023, a result welcomed by environmentalists as benefiting the Amazon. Official monitoring figures cited in the report show forest loss fell 42 per cent over the past year and deforestation dropped 71 per cent below its 2022 level, reaching its lowest since records began in 1988. Greenpeace Brazil called it a win for democracy maintaining protection commitments. The decline is linked to PPCDAm revival strengthening monitoring and enforcement. Challenges remain as rival challenges the result and right-wing parties gain Congress representation limiting environmental legislation passage while wildfires, illegal logging and El Niño drought conditions persist.
items.title: Lula's Reelection Tied to Amazon Deforestation Decline

items.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation reviewed aviation safety and operational readiness as Cyclone Arnab is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, with winds of 125–135 kmph and gusts up to 150 kmph per IMD. Airlines including Air India, IndiGo and Akasa Air reported cancellations or suspensions at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Rajahmundry; the ministry said cancellation figures were provisional.
items.title: Aviation ministry suspends flights at three Andhra airports ahead of Cyclone Arnab

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration seized food articles worth Rs 25. 53 lakh from 14 establishments during a two-day inspection drive on October 25 and 26. In Mumbai it took dry fruits and roasted almonds valued at Rs 6,78,900 from Curated Foods and chips worth Rs 20,730 from Ananta Food Products for labelling violations. Separately in Thane it seized 7,566 packets of expired packaged food worth Rs 6. 88 lakh from Cloudstore Retail Pvt Ltd after the firm failed to produce disposal records. Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said strict action would continue against operators selling unsafe products.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Seizes Dry Fruits, Chips and Expired Food Across State

items.summary: The Congress’ Keralam unit tendered an unconditional apology over a social media post that called on Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to resign. The message was deleted within hours amid criticism and followed remarks the CJI made while hearing a plea about restrictions in Delhi during protests against the resignation demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: Congress Keralam Unit Apologises for Post Targeting CJI

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh authorities have evacuated at least 89,000 people from vulnerable coastal areas as Cyclone Arnab intensified over the Bay of Bengal and was expected to make landfall early Wednesday. The India Meteorological Department classified it a very severe cyclonic storm. Senior official Prakhar Jain said the storm could reach the coast between 2 am and 4 am on Wednesday, with winds possibly reaching 140 kmph at landfall.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh Evacuates Nearly 90,000 Ahead of Cyclone Arnab Landfall
